newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slumps under month-end dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slumps under month-end dlr demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee slipped to 35.69/70 per dollar on Wednesday after opening the day steady at 35.65/66, dealers said.
The rupee was steady until forenoon when a major state-run bank stepped in to buy dollars. This bank's buying, in phases, pushed the rupee down to 35.70 level, dealers said.
They reported deals at a low of 35.70 on Wednesday.
After this bank's exit, other banks continued to buy.
"The 35.67/68 level was twice tested and broke through the third time," said a dealer at a state-run bank. He attributed the pressure to bunching of some major outward remittances.
Another dealer said an Indian financial institution also had a large overseas remittance on Wednesday.
"The Reserve Bank of India was conspicuous by its absence today," said a dealer at a Bombay forex brokerage.
The rupee continued to extend its gains in the forward dollar market. "Most of it was inter-bank (deals)," said the chief dealer at a foreign bank.
He said the soft premia reflected a sharp fall in overnight call money rates rather than forward dollar sales by exporters.
Some dealers said the rupee did not look like gaining even after month-end accumulated dollar demand subsides on Thursday, the last day of the month. But others were not sure.
"As soon as he goes away, the sentiment is affected," said a dealer, referring to a leading Calcutta-based bank.
